title: Bridged handover and stability playbook for latency echoes
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook documents the rapid handover, triage, containment, and customer communication patterns for persistent or oscillatory latency incidents we call "latency echoes" (periodic or reappearing latency spikes across one or more regions). It is intended for on‑call engineers, bridge operators, and incident commanders.

Goals:
- Restore customer latency SLOs within the Restoration SLO (see SLO table).
- Keep customer communications clear, consistent, and brand-safe.
- Preserve evidence for postmortem and regulatory audit.

Scope:
- Applies to Redwood inference runtime services (frontend API, router, model workers, cache layer) across hosted and dedicated deployments.
- Excludes planned maintenance (see maintenance runbook).

Ownership and roles:
1) Primary on‑call (first responder) — responsible for initial triage, evidence collection, and staging mitigation.
2) Bridge operator — runs the coordinated communication bridge, timestamps messages, and triggers exec notifications.
3) Incident commander (IC) — owns restoration decisions, rollbacks, and customer communications for severity escalations.
4) SRE lead — leads capacity or routing fixes; works with infra and runtime teams.

Severity definitions (quick reference):
- Sev2 (Degraded): Significant latency regressions for >5% customers or 3 consecutive minutes of 2x median latency.
- Sev1 (Partial outage): Majority of requests >3x median latency or errors >1% absolute above baseline.
- Sev0 (Major outage): Complete or near complete service unavailability.

Detection and alerting patterns:
- Primary signals: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, queue depth, request duration heatmaps, KV cache hit ratio.
- Alert rule examples (Prometheus):
  - expr: increase(api_request_errors[1m]) > 50
  - expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)) > 2.5
- When an alert fires, the primary on‑call must acknowledge within 2 minutes.

First 10 minutes (fast path):
1) Acknowledge the alert and create an incident page in Confluence (timestamp + initial hypothesis).
2) Capture scope: which region(s), model types, routes, customers affected.
3) Run the minimal evidence checklist (commands below) and paste outputs to the incident page.
4) If impact meets Sev2/Sev1 criteria, escalate to bridge operator and IC.

Minimal evidence checklist (copy/paste commands):
- Check API gateway errors and upstream latency: 
  curl -sS https://metrics-api.internal/query?expr=api_request_errors | jq .
- Snapshot p95/p99 for last 15m: 
  promql: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(api_request_duration_seconds_bucket[15m])) by (service,region))
- Inspect router queue depths: 
  ssh router-prod-01 -- sudo /opt/bin/queue-inspect --service model-router --hours 1
- Check KV cache hit rate: 
  promql: sum(rate(kv_cache_hits[5m])) / sum(rate(kv_cache_lookups[5m]))

Triage decision ladder (quick):
- If a single region is affected and router queue depth is high: prioritize scaling router workers and evicting noisy tenants.
- If KV cache hit ratio drops suddenly: check KV store latency and recent invalidation/flush events.
- If model worker CPU/GPU utilization is saturated: shift routing to warm spare pools and enable reduced-batch fallthrough.
- If errors are rising with stable latency: suspect dependency errors (auth, datastore).

Containment and mitigation playbook (operational steps):
1) Short-term mitigations (under 15 minutes):
   - Activate traffic shaping by customer tier: divert non‑critical traffic to lower priority pools.
   - Increase router concurrency and reduce batch sizes to lower tail latency.
   - Enable KV caching warmup skip for high‑fanout prompts.
2) Mid-term mitigations (15–60 minutes):
   - Scale dedicated pools (trigger autoscale policy override).
   - Apply targeted canary routing to unaffected model variants.
   - Pin stable model version for critical tenants (avoid in‑flight rollouts).
3) Long-term mitigation (>60 minutes):
   - Perform rolling restart of router nodes with controlled draining.
   - Recompile hot kernels for problem architecture (coordinate with runtime team).

Rollback and abort criteria:
- Immediate rollback to last known stable model version if generation errors or hallucination regressions accompany latency spikes.
- Abort any capacity reductions or cache flushes that increase p99 by >15%.

Communication templates (copy, adapt):
Internal bridge initial post (short):
- Title: Incident | Latency echoes | [region] | [service]
- Body: We are investigating increased latency in [region]. Initial scope: [x]% customers affected; p95 up from [A]ms to [B]ms. Primary hypothesis: [brief]. On‑call: [name]. IC: [name].

Customer status template (public-facing):
- Subject: Redwood status — degraded performance for inference (region)
- Body: We are currently investigating degraded performance affecting inference in [region]. Some requests may experience elevated latency. Our teams are actively triaging and applying mitigations. We will provide an update within 30 minutes or when the situation materially changes. We apologize for the disruption.

Customer status template (detailed for enterprise customers):
- Title: Enterprise notice — elevated latency impacting inference throughput
- Body: Impact: Customers in [region/tenant] may experience 2–3x latency increases. Mitigations in progress: traffic shaping, routing to warm pools, and model pinning for critical tenants. ETA for next update: 30 minutes. If you require targeted support, contact your CSM or reply to this message; we have opened a priority channel.

On‑call rotation and handoff checklist (5 minute walk):
- Outgoing oncall must leave: current incident list, bridges open (links), last 3 evidence snapshots, active mitigations, and any outstanding asks for infra/runtime.
- Incoming oncall must: confirm bridge access, review evidence snapshots, acknowledge responsibility in the incident page, and confirm communication cadence.
- Handoff marker: add a single sentence to the incident page: "Handoff complete — outgoing: NAME @ HH:MM, incoming: NAME @ HH:MM"

Game day run (quarterly, suggested script):
1) Objective: Validate handover timing, cross-team bridge execution, and targeted rollback mechanics for a simulated latency echo caused by cache invalidation.
2) Scope: 1 region, 2 services (router, cache), 1 enterprise tenant simulated.
3) Pre‑work: create deliberate metric anomalies (prometheus replay), prepare synthetic load generator, pre-assign roles (IC, bridge, SRE, runtime).
4) Execution: 30 minute active window following fast path steps; evaluate time to acknowledgement, first mitigation, and customer message issuance.
5) Post-game: collect metrics and a short playbook after-action note with 3 concrete improvements.

Evidence and metric collection requirements for postmortem:
- Required artifacts: incident timeline (minute resolution), Prometheus snapshots (p50/p95/p99), router queue traces, kernel logs from affected model workers, layout of traffic shifts (routing config diffs), customer complaints/tickets linked.
- Storage: upload artifacts to incident bucket s3://incidents/YYYYMMDD-latency-echo and link in the page.

Postmortem and action item template (minimum):
- Summary (1 paragraph)
- Timeline (table of events with hh:mm)
- Root cause hypothesis and evidence
- Contributing factors
- Action items (owner, due date, verification steps)
- Severity review and SLO credit decision

SLO and alert thresholds (table):
| Service | SLO (monthly) | Alert (p95) | Immediate action |
| API gateway | p99 < 1.2s | p95 > 500ms for 5m | Run fast path & bridge |
| Router | p95 < 300ms | p95 > 700ms for 3m | Scale router & reduce batch |
| Model worker | p95 < 200ms | p95 > 600ms | Reroute to warm pools |

Contact matrix (short):
- Oncall team channel: #oncall-ops
- Bridge channel: #incident-bridge
- Exec notify (if Sev1 for >30m): @oncall-lead, @cto

Runbook governance and versioning:
- This document is authoritative for latency echo incidents. Minor updates may be made by SRE lead; major changes require IC and product review.
- Versioning: update the top of the incident page with the playbook version and changelog line.

Appendix A — Example incident evidence snippet (pasteable):
{
  "timestamp": "2026-01-09T14:02:00Z",
  "p95_ms": 1250,
  "router_queue_depth": 412,
  "kv_cache_hit": 0.63
}

Appendix B — Quick links:
- Routing control console: https://ops-console.internal/routing
- Incident bucket pattern: s3://incidents/YYYYMMDD-<short-id>
- Playbook author and reviewer list (see metadata).

Frequently asked decisions (FAQ):
Q: When should we call the customer success desk directly?
A: For enterprise tenants with active incidents and SLA exposure (Sev1 > 15 minutes) escalate to Customer Success for direct outreach.

Q: Can we use aggressive cache flush as a first mitigation?
A: No — avoid full cache flushes unless validated in a staging replay; prefer targeted invalidation.

Contact and escalation quick roster:
- Oncall lead: oncall-lead@redwood.com
- SRE lead: sre-lead@redwood.com
- Runtime engineering: runtime-team@redwood.com

End of playbook.
